assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 225% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, driven by a loss of U.S. measles elimination status.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 1003% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, indicating a significant rise in activity.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, though the number of cases this year is slightly lower than last year.
Polio cases in the US are peaking with a circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 outbreak reported in Syria, as noted by WHO.
Global flu test positivity is rising, with US flu hospital admissions up 55% over the past month, though the disease is currently at baseline activity.
Whooping cough cases in the US are rising with a 52% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, indicating a growing trend.
Respiratory syncytial virus cases in the US are at baseline with hospital admissions up 57% over the past month, though the disease is not currently peaking.
COVID-19 hospital admissions in the US are at baseline with a 13% increase over the past month, though the disease is not currently peaking.
Malaria cases in the US are at baseline with a slight increase in reported cases this year, but news coverage and Wikipedia readership are both rising.
Norovirus news coverage is rising, but Wikipedia readership remains stable.
Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a slight increase, but there are new cases reported in Switzerland.
West Nile virus cases in the US are rising sharply, with a significant increase in reported cases this year.
Human metapneumovirus news coverage is rising significantly, but Wikipedia readership is stable.
Avian influenza cases in the US are at baseline, but there are new reports of human infections linked to dairy cattle.
Cholera news coverage is rising, but Wikipedia readership is low.
